headline: A 2015 House resolution, voted down, would have directed the President to pull U.S. troops deployed to Iraq or Syria since August 2014 out of those countries.
what_it_does: If adopted, this concurrent resolution would have told the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces sent to Iraq or Syria on or after August 7, 2014. Troops needed to protect U.S. diplomatic facilities and personnel would have been exempt. The removal would have been due within 30 days, or by December 31, 2015, or sooner if the President found it could safely be done.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. military members deployed to Iraq or Syria since August 7, 2014
who_it_affects.how: They would have been required to leave Iraq and Syria, except those protecting U.S. diplomatic facilities and personnel.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. diplomatic staff in Iraq and Syria
who_it_affects.how: Military units guarding them would have been allowed to stay, so their protection would have continued under the exemption.
The President would have had to carry out the removal within the set deadlines, or determine that it could not yet be done safely.
